items.title: 16.9 Resistor ke zariye discharge hote capacitor ka exponential decay (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 16.9 with Figs. 16.14-16.16, the box and Example 16.10 (PDF 78-80).

blocks.text: Pichhle hisse mein Fig. 16.13 (a) mein resistor ke zariye discharge hone wala RC circuit dekha. Us ke charge aur waqt ka graph Fig. 16.14 mein hai. Charge Q waqt t ke saath exponentially (pehle tezi se, phir aahista) kam hota hai. Aam zabaan mein exponential ka matlab hai bohat tezi se barhna ya ghatna. Riyazi (math) mein exponential function woh hai jis mein variable power (exponent) mein ho:

blocks.alt: Discharge hote capacitor ke charge aur waqt ka graph: curve oonchai se shuru ho kar pehle tezi se aur phir ahista ahista girta hai aur waqt ke mehwar ke qareeb hamwar ho jata hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 16.14: Discharge hote capacitor ka charge aur waqt (kitab ki Figure 16.14 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.text: Yahan a constant aur x exponent (variable) hai. RC circuit mein discharge hone wale capacitor ka aam exponential decay formula yeh hai:
Yahan x koi bhi miqdar (charge, voltage ya current) hai waqt t par.

items: x₀ = t = 0 par us miqdar ki shuru wali qeemat.
RC = time constant (τ), jo batata hai ke capacitor kitni jaldi discharge hota hai.
e = aik riyazi constant (Euler's number), natural logarithm (logₑ ya ln) ka base; is ki qeemat taqreeban 2.718 hai.

blocks.text: Power mein minus (−t/RC) batata hai ke miqdar waqt ke saath exponentially kam hoti hai.
Eq. 16.43 se kisi bhi waqt t par charge, voltage aur current ki kami yun likhi jati hai:

blocks.latex: Q = Q_0e^{-t/RC},\; V = V_0e^{-t/RC} \;\text{and}\; I = I_0e^{-t/RC}.
blocks.text_alt: Q = Q₀e^(−t/RC), V = V₀e^(−t/RC) and I = I₀e^(−t/RC).

blocks.text: Teenon ke graph shuru mein bohat dhalwan (steep, tez discharge) hote hain aur waqt ke saath chapte (flat) hote jate hain, yani discharge sust hota jata hai. Fig. 16.15 charge ka graph dikhati hai.

blocks.alt: Qo se shuru hone wala charge aur waqt ka graph. Pehle waqfe t ke baad charge Q hai. Baad mein, utne hi lambe waqfe t mein, charge Qo' se Q' tak girta hai, jo kahin chhoti kami hai. Dashed lakeerein charge ke mehwar par Q, Qo' aur Q' dikhati hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 16.15: Barabar waqfon t mein charge ki kami (kitab ki Figure 16.15 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.text: Shuru mein charge Q₀ (t = 0) hai aur waqt t baad Q reh jata hai. Baad mein kisi aur lamhe charge Q₀′ ho, to utne hi waqt t baad woh Q′ reh jata hai. Shuru mein kami (Q₀ − Q) thi, baad mein kami (Q₀′ − Q′) hai, jo pehle se kam hai. Wajah: har barabar waqfe mein charge apne maujooda hisse ka aik jaisa fraction khota hai, is liye charge kam ho to kami bhi kam hoti hai.

Charge ka ghatna tanki se patle pipe ke zariye pani nikalne jaisa hai. Pani ki satah aur dabao (pressure) charge aur voltage jaise hain, aur pani ke bahao ki raftar current jaisi. Shuru mein satah oonchi hai, dabao zyada hai aur pani tez nikalta hai. Satah girne se dabao kam hota hai aur bahao sust ho jata hai.

blocks.title: For your information
blocks.text: Exponential functions physics ke bohat se mamlaat ko sahi sahi bayan karte hain, jaise radioactive decay, jahan kisi cheez ke badalne ki raftar us ki maujooda miqdar par seedha munhasir hoti hai.
Time constant ka kirdar
Time constant RC = τ capacitor ke resistance ke zariye charge aur discharge hone mein bohat ahem hai. Capacitor ke charge ka exponential decay yeh hai:
t = RC rakhein to aik time constant baad bacha charge milta hai:
e = 2.718 rakhein:
Is se time constant ki definition milti hai:

blocks.title: Time constant
blocks.text: Time constant (τ) woh waqt hai jis mein shuru ka charge Q₀ gir kar taqreeban 0.37 Q₀ reh jata hai.

Yani aik time constant baad charge apni shuru ki qeemat ka 37% reh jata hai; voltage aur current bhi utne hi girte hain. Chhota time constant matlab circuit jaldi react karta hai, bara time constant matlab aahista (Fig. 16.16). Ab woh waqt t₁/₂ nikalte hain jis mein charge Q₀ ka aadha (half) reh jaye. Q = ½Q₀ rakhein:

blocks.alt: Qo se shuru hone wala charge aur waqt ka graph. Dashed lakeerein dikhati hain ke 0.69RC ke baad charge Qo ka aadha aur aik time constant RC ke baad 0.37Qo reh jata hai; dono waqt origin se waqt ke mehwar par teeron se dikhaye gaye hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 16.16: Charge 0.69RC mein Qo ka aadha aur aik time constant RC mein 0.37Qo reh jata hai (kitab ki Figure 16.16 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.text: Natural logarithm (ln) ki definition se dono taraf ln lein:
Calculator se ln(2) = 0.693, is liye −ln(2) = −0.69. Yeh qeemat Eq. (16.44) mein rakhein:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab likhti hai '−ln(2) = −0.6' aur 'Eq. 4.45' mein rakhein. Sahi: ln 2 = 0.693, yani −ln(2) ≈ −0.69 (agli line mein kitab khud 0.69 hi istemal karti hai), aur qeemat Eq. (16.44) mein rakhi jati hai; is chapter mein Eq. 4.45 nahi.
Yeh Fig. 16.16 ke graph mein dikhaya gaya hai: 0.69RC par charge ½Q₀ aur RC par 0.37Q₀.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab 'Fig. 4.17' likhti hai; is chapter mein aisi koi figure nahi. Murad Fig. 16.16 hai.

blocks.title: Asaan alfaaz mein
blocks.text: Half time t₁/₂ = 0.69RC time constant RC se thora kam hai, kyunke aadha (0.5) hona 0.37 tak girne se pehle aata hai. Isi tarah har agle 0.69RC mein charge phir aadha ho jata hai: ½, ¼, ⅛ ...

blocks.title: Example 16.10
blocks.problem: RC circuit mein R = 1 kΩ, C = 100 μF aur V₀ = 10 V hai. 0.2 s baad capacitor par voltage nikalein.
steps: Time constant: τ = RC = 1000 Ω × 100 × 10⁻⁶ F = 0.1 s
Maloom karna hai: t = 0.2 s par V
Voltage ka decay formula: V = V₀e⁻ᵗᐟᴿᶜ

blocks.prompt: Example 16.10 ke circuit mein voltage ko 5 V tak girne mein kitna waqt lagega?
blocks.explanation: 5 V, 10 V ka aadha hai, is liye t = t₁/₂ = 0.69RC = 0.69 × 0.1 s = 0.069 s.

blocks.text: Mukhtasar khulasa

items: Charge, voltage aur current: x = x₀e⁻ᵗᐟᴿᶜ.
Aik time constant RC baad 0.37 (37%) bachta hai.
Half time: t₁/₂ = 0.69RC; chhota RC = tez decay.
